title: a tour of creative systems ecosystem
content:
a 3 minute tour of the course home

explore creative systems course

I spent this past month creating and teaching the live run of my creative systems course — which took up all the RAM space in my brain and set off all the creative firepower/fireworks I’m currently in possession of. this class has felt like my vessel for everything I’ve integrated in this last decade around the intersection between creative & business work.


ready for asychronous, self-paced study

last night, I transitioned the course dashboard to its asynchronous study version. I thought I’d share the structure of the course experience, assignments, and the different community/creative experiments I’m cooking up.

something I’ve realized over many years of teaching courses (most of which are currently inactive) is that in order for me to not abandon a project (regardless of whether or not it makes me money), I must keep it alive. I must keep it interesting for me to tend to, otherwise the course is dead to me, and I’ll feel too disconnected and disembodied from it to keep sharing it. this is why I want my courses to feel like garden ecosystems — deeper worlds inside my website world. I’m sure that the course dashboard will evolve over the next months and years, which is why I’ve documented it here.
